payload.name: SearchShortPhrasesWithBaseNoun
payload.description: When a question asks for a short attribute like a motto, slogan, nickname, or title, include the standalone base noun in keyword searches and try a semantic/hybrid search if the exact phrase misses.
content: If the query asks about a short named attribute (motto, slogan, nickname, title), add the bare noun (e.g., 'motto') as a keyword in addition to any full phrase like 'family motto'.

When the first keyword search does not return a memory containing that attribute word, re-run with the base word alone and also perform a semantic or hybrid search before concluding no information is available.

solves: The failure occurred because a keyword search for 'family motto' missed an existing memory containing 'family's motto' — the possessive form blocked exact phrase matching. Future questions about short attributes such as a motto, slogan, nickname, or title face the same risk when the stored text uses a possessive or inflected variant. This rule applies when the target is a retrievable short phrase; it does not apply when the answer must be synthesized from multiple facts.
